# Documentation Review

## 1. Claims match the current source tree

Fail.

- `docs/reference/labels.md` documents label-management commands and issue-update flags absent from `cli.rs`.
- `docs/reference/storage-format.md` claims older repositories may be automatically migrated and have their format marker bumped. The storage loader accepts older versions unchanged; only the explicit lifecycle-timestamp migration exists.

The five findings from the most recent review run are resolved, including the control-plane layout defect.

## 2. Adopter surface versus dogfood configuration

Pass.

Repository-specific types, namespaces, rules, templates, item kinds, and gates are identified as repository-local configuration or clearly marked worked examples. No dogfood value is presented as a `jit init` default.

## 3. Current behavior only

Fail.

Future-facing product narration remains in the root README, installation guide, and guarantees concept. Historical replacement and legacy-alias narration also remains in worked configurations and references.

## 4. No hardcoded counts that silently rot

Pass.

The remaining numeric counts are command output, limits, configuration values, or illustrative data rather than hand-maintained product totals.

## 5. Links and referenced paths resolve

Pass.

Repository-relative Markdown targets and anchors resolve. All actual addressable-item citations resolve through `jit item show`; `@/issue/REQ-01` is explicitly presented as a parse-error example rather than a citation. `jit validate --json` reports zero errors.

## 6. Content-standards conformance

Fail.

No prohibited non-Mermaid diagram or definite plain-text mathematics defect remains. Plain-text box-drawing blocks are permitted directory trees or CLI output. The current-behavior narration findings below violate the present-state documentation standard.

## Findings

1. **F1 — Labels reference documents a nonexistent CLI surface.** [docs/reference/labels.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/labels.md:328) uses nonexistent `--replace-label`; line 355 uses nonexistent `jit label suggest`; lines 384 and 479–517 document nonexistent namespace-management, audit, fix, and removal commands; line 639 uses `jit graph downstream` correctly as an alias, but line 702 adds nonexistent `jit label schema`. The actual label surface is only `jit label namespaces` and `jit label values`, while issue labels are changed with `--label` and `--remove-label`. Remediation: rewrite every command and workflow example around the exposed CLI, replacing a label with paired `--remove-label`/`--label`, and remove unsupported discovery, mutation, audit, fix, and schema claims.
2. **F2 — Storage reference claims automatic format migration that is not implemented.** [docs/reference/storage-format.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/storage-format.md:285) says writing with a newer binary may migrate older data and bump `schema_version`. `ensure_supported_index_version` accepts an older index unchanged, and no generic automatic migration performs this bump. Remediation: state that equal and older supported versions are accepted unchanged, newer repository versions are rejected, and name only explicit migration commands that currently exist.
3. **F3 — Root README advertises unspecified future product work.** [README.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/README.md:240) tells adopters to expect new features and bug fixes before 1.0. Remediation: replace the roadmap-style statement with the product’s current stability/version status.
4. **F4 — Installation guide presents an in-flight publication state.** [INSTALL.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/INSTALL.md:211) labels the npm installation path “After Publishing,” describing a future distribution state. Remediation: document the currently available installation method directly; remove the npm-global pathway if it is not currently published.
5. **F5 — Guarantees document advertises unimplemented future capabilities.** [docs/concepts/guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:121) says the event log supports future undo/replay capabilities, and line 158 advertises undo, replay, and time-travel debugging. No adopter-facing commands implement these capabilities. Remediation: describe the current append-only audit and query behavior only, removing roadmap items.
6. **F6 — Research worked configuration narrates a historical configuration replacement.** [docs/examples/research/templates.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/examples/research/templates.toml:9) calls the template model a replacement for an “old flat planning config block.” Remediation: state directly that this file declares the research planning bracket and demonstrates domain-agnostic templates.
7. **F7 — SDD worked configuration narrates a historical configuration replacement.** [docs/examples/sdd/templates.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/examples/sdd/templates.toml:9) repeats the “replacement for the old” transition narrative. Remediation: describe only the current SDD template and the graph it instantiates.
8. **F8 — Command grammar uses historical framing for current aliases.** [docs/reference/cli-command-grammar.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-command-grammar.md:160) calls `pass`, `pass-all`, `check`, and `check-all` “legacy” verbs. Remediation: list them simply as accepted aliases of the canonical current commands.
9. **F9 — CLI reference uses historical framing for a current alias.** [docs/reference/cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1806) calls `check` a “Legacy alias.” Remediation: state directly that `check` is an alias of `status`.

Total findings: 9
